MINUTES

  CITY COUNCIL MEETING

  SEPTEMBER 26, 2017

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order
by MAYOR ZERUNYAN at 7:03 p.m. in the Council Chamber, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North,
Rolling Hills Estates.

ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan

City Council Members Absent:  Zuckerman (excused)

City Staff Present: City Manager Doug Prichard
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Greg Grammer
  Planning Director David Wahba
  Administrative Services Director Mike Whitehead
  Community Services Director Andy Clark
  Assistant to the City Manager Alexa Davis
  City Clerk Heidi Luce

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF led the audience in the Pledge of Allegiance.

CEREMONIAL ITEMS

MAYOR ZERUNYAN shared with those present the certificates of recognition that were
presented to the City by Assembly Member Al Muratsuchi, Senator Ben Allen and Los
Angeles County Supervisor Janice Hahn at the City’s 60th Anniversary Celebration event on
September 23, 2017. He also thanked the elected officials and their representatives for their
participation in the event.

5.  ROUTINE MATTERS

A.  SPECIAL CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 12, 2017

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ.

  TO APPROVE THE SPECIAL CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 12,
  2017 AS PRESENTED.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
SEPTEMBER 26, 2017
 B.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 12, 2017

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL.

  TO APPROVE THE CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 12, 2017 AS
  PRESENTED.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

C.  ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 18, 2017

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ.

  TO APPROVE THE ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 18,
  2017 AS PRESENTED.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

D.  ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 19, 2017

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL.

  TO APPROVE THE ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 19,
  2017 AS PRESENTED.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

E.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS – SEPTEMBER

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ.

  TO APPROVE WARRANTS 58965 THROUGH 59001 FOR A GRAND TOTAL
  AMOUNT OF $367,383.85 WITH PROPER AUDIT.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan

6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

  The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority
  consent of the City Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless
  good cause is shown by a member prior to the roll call vote. (Items removed will be
  considered under New Business.)

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ.

  TO APPROVE ITEMS A-E.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
SEPTEMBER 26, 2017
 A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

  Reading in full of all ordinances and resolutions presented for consideration to the
  City Council will be waived and all such ordinances and resolutions will be read by
  title only.

  APPROVED.

B.  AUGUST 2017 SCHEDULE OF INVESTMENTS

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

C.  AUGUST 2017 MONTHLY REVENUE AND EXPENDITURE REPORT

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

D.  AUTHORITY TO DESTROY ORIGINAL DAMAGED RECORDS

  APPROVED.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

E.  SECOND AMENDMENT TO THE PROPOSAL TO CONDUCT AN INITIAL STUDY AND
  MITIGATED NEGATIVE DECLARATION FOR THE PALOS VERDES PIPELINE
  PROJECT.

  APPROVED AMENDMENT.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan

7.  AUDIENCE  ITEMS  NOT  ON  THE  AGENDA/WRITTEN  AND  ORAL
  COMMUNICATIONS

  Residents Lisa Turek, Cindy Martin and Jim Gardner addressed the City council to
  express concern regarding coyotes in the City.

  Following public comment and with City Council concurrence, the following direction
  was provided to staff:

  THE CITY COUNCIL DIRECTED STAFF TO AGENDIZE THIS MATTER FOR
  DISCUSSION AT A FUTURE CITY COUNCIL MEETING.

A.  SBCCOG PRESENTATION REGARDING DUES STRUCTURE

  Jacki Bacharach, Executive Director, SBCCOG and Christian Horvath, Council
  Member, Redondo Beach/SBCCOG Board Member addressed the City Council
  regarding the SBCCOG dues structure, the formula that is used to calculate the dues,
  the various SBCCOG initiatives and the SBCCOG work program.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
SEPTEMBER 26, 2017
   MAYOR ZERUNYAN expressed concern regarding the disparity in the formula when
  comparing the dues paid by smaller cities to the dues paid by the larger cities. He
  noted that per capita, the smaller cities pay exponentially more.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ  commented  that  she  concurs  with  MAYOR
  ZERUNYAN’S comments.

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL commented that the SBCCOG has played a critical
  role in many regional initiatives including having an impact on the allocation of
  Measure M funds and the homelessness initiative.

  Following discussion and with City Council concurrence, the following action was
  taken:

  THE CITY COUNCIL REQUESTED THAT THE SBCCOG STEERING COMMITTEE
  UNDERTAKE REVIEW OF THE DUES STRUCTURE PROCESS AND OFFERED TO
  ASSIST IN THE REVIEW PROCESS.

8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS/MEETINGS

  NONE

9.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  ADJOURNED PLANNING COMMISSION MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 11, 2017

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ.

  TO RECEIVE AND FILE THE ADJOURNED PLANNING COMMISSION MINUTES
  OF SEPTEMBER 11, 2017.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

B.  PLANNING COMMISSION CONSIDERS POLICY TO ALLOW METAL STANDING-SEAM
  ROOFS ON RESIDENTIAL HOMES IN THE DAPPLEGRAY LANES NEIGHBORHOOD
  AND POSSIBLY CITY-WIDE

  Planning Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per agenda material).

  In response to MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF, Planning Director Wahba stated that metal
  standing-seam roofs are typically more expensive than many of the roofing materials
  currently allowed in City; and they are fire retardant, but may experience heat-related
  issues in a fire. Also in response to MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF, Planning Director Wahba
  stated that in its discussion on this topic, the Planning Commission’s inclination was
  to consider requests for these types of roofs on a case-by-case basis.

  Residents Keith Khorey and Paul Moylan addressed the City Council in support of
  allowing metal standing-seam roofs on residential homes in Rolling Hills Estates.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
SEPTEMBER 26, 2017
   Planning Director Wahba noted that City staff received an e-mail from Mrs. Glicksman
  in opposition to allowing metal standing-seam roof.

  MAYOR ZERUNYAN commented that the City typically looks to the individual home
  owners associations in each neighborhood for input on these types of matters. He
  suggested referring this matter back to the Planning Commission for further
  discussion with the community and to receive input from the HOA’s; and bring back to
  the City Council as part of the Policy Development Session in 2018.

  Following discussion and with City Council concurrence, the following action was
  taken:

  DIRECTED STAFF/PLANNING COMMISSION TO CONTINUE REVIEW OF THIS
  MATTER  AND  BRING  THE  STAFF/PLANNING  COMMISSION
  RECOMMENDATION TO THE CITY COUNCIL AS PART OF THE POLICY
  DEVELOPMENT SESSION IN 2018.

C.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 18, 2017

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL.

  TO RECEIVE AND FILE THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES
  OF SEPTEMBER 18, 2017.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

D.  PAVEMENT MANAGEMENT SYSTEM 2017 REPORT AND APPROVAL OF PROJECT
  LIST FOR RMRA FUND ELIGIBILITY

  Recommendation:  That the City Council receive and file the 2017 Pavement
  Management System Report and approve a recommended project list and associated
  budget adjustments to meet the funding eligibility guidelines for receipt of Road
  Maintenance and Rehabilitation Account (RMRA) funds.

  Assistant City Manager Grammer and Roxanne Hughes, Willdan Engineering provided
  a staff report and reviewed the 2017 Pavement Management System Report (as per
  agenda material).

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF

  TO RECEIVE AND FILE THE 2017 PAVEMENT MANAGEMENT SYSTEM
  REPORT AND APPROVE A RECOMMENDED PROJECT LIST AND ASSOCIATED
  BUDGET ADJUSTMENTS TO MEET THE FUNDING ELIGIBILITY GUIDELINES
  FOR RECEIPT OF ROAD MAINTENANCE AND REHABILITATION ACCOUNT
  (RMRA) FUNDS.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
SEPTEMBER 26, 2017
 E.  AUTHORIZATION TO SOLICIT BIDS FOR THE 2017-18 STREET RESURFACING
  PROJECT

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the attached specifications and bid
  documents and authorize the solicitation of bids for the 2017-18 Resurfacing Project
  on Various City Streets.

  Assistant City Manager Grammer provided a staff report (as per agenda material).

  In response to COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL, Assistant City Manager Grammer
  confirmed HR Green’s estimate for the project at $1,350,000 exceeds the amount that
  was budgeted for the project by $350,000. He noted that the bid document is
  structured in such a way that there are additive/alternative items so that the City
  Council will have the option to keep within the budgeted amount.

  In response to MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF, Assistant City Manager Grammer stated that
  the bids will be due on October 26, 2017 with the intent to award the bid in November
  and the work commencing in the spring.

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ

  TO APPROVE THE SPECIFICATIONS AND BID DOCUMENTS AND AUTHORIZE
  THE SOLICITATION OF BIDS FOR THE 2017-18 RESURFACING PROJECT ON
  VARIOUS CITY STREETS.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan

10.  OLD BUSINESS

A.  AUTHORIZATION TO SOLICIT BIDS FOR THE 2017-18 STORM DRAIN PIPE
  REHABILITATION PROJECT (YEAR 1)

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the attached specifications and bid
  documents and authorize the solicitation of bids for the 2017-18 Storm Drain Pipe
  Rehabilitation Project (Year 1).

  Assistant City Manager Grammer provided a staff report (as per agenda material).

  In response to COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ, Assistant City Manager Grammer stated
  that residents in the Strawberry Lane neighborhood are contributing to the project in
  order to install a more aesthetically pleasing drain.

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF

  TO APPROVE THE SPECIFICATIONS AND BID DOCUMENTS AND AUTHORIZE
  THE SOLICITATION OF BIDS FOR THE 2017-18 STORM DRAIN PIPE
  REHABILITATION PROJECT (YEAR 1)

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  6
SEPTEMBER 26, 2017
 B.  PUBLIC OUTREACH ENHANCEMENT

  Recommendation: That the City Council engage Tripepi Smith for web site review and
  a City Council workshop and provide staff with further direction.

  Assistant to the City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per agenda material).

  In response COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ, Assistant to the City Manager Davis stated
  that Tripepi Smith will assess the user experience and provide recommendations,
  within the limitations of the City’s current website provider, for enhancing accessibility
  and the user experience.

  In response to MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF, Assistant to the City Manager Davis stated
  that city staff does the all of the content update on the City’s web site; and as
  opportunities are identified, the intern starting in the coming weeks will assist in
  implementing the recommendations.

  MAYOR ZERUNYAN commented that the consultant identified is highly recommended,
  extremely competent and will do a good job.

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL commented that his experience working with similar
  cities, as indicated on his resume, will be a benefit in his working with Rolling Hills
  Estates.

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ.

  TO ENGAGE TRIPEPI SMITH FOR WEB SITE REVIEW AND A CITY COUNCIL
  WORKSHOP ON PUBLIC ENGAGEMENT

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan

11.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

  City Attorney Davis commented, with regard to the coyote issue brought up during
  public comment, that there are some legal issues associated with controlling coyotes
  and suggested that the City proceed prudently on this policy issue.

12.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS:  This item provides the
  opportunity for Members of the City Council to provide information and reports to other
  Members of the City Council and/or the public on any issues or activities of currently
  active Council Committees, ad hoc committees, regional or state-wide governmental
  associations, special districts and/or joint powers authorities and their various
  committees on which Members of the City Council might serve or have an interest, which
  are not otherwise agendized.

A.  MAYOR ZERUNYAN reported that the City Council, along with staff, attended the
  League of California Cities Annual Conference & Expo in Sacramento September 13-
  15, 2017 and learned valuable information during the conference. He also reported
  that the Contract Cities Fall Conference will be held this coming weekend.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  7
SEPTEMBER 26, 2017
 B.  MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF reported that the Holiday Parade Committee met on Monday.
  The date for this year’s parade is Saturday, December 2nd at 6:00 p.m.

13.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS: This item provides the opportunity for Members of the
  City Council to request information on currently pending projects and/or issues of public
  concern, direct that an item be agendized for future consideration and/or make
  announcements of interest to the public.

A.  APPOINTMENT OF GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEMBERS

  MAYOR ZERUNYAN commented that the City was fortunate to have received
  applications from many well qualified applicants for appointment to the General Plan
  Advisory Committee (GPAC).

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL

  TO APPOINT JOHN ADDLEMAN, WARREN ARATA, JUDY BAYER, KAREN
  BURESH, GERRY CARRESE, CHRISTOPHER CORMAN, JOAN FRIEDMAN,
  RITU PORTUGAL, SUZY SEAMANS, VICKI SHINN, CARRIE SILVANO AND
  DEBBY STEGURA T0 THE GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan

B.  APPOINTMENT OF PLANNING COMMISSION MEMBER

  MAYOR ZERUNYAN commented that the City was again, fortunate to have received
  several well qualified applicants for appointment to Planning Commission vacancy.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL

  TO APPOINT RICHARD EDLER T0 THE PLANNING COMMISSION.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan

C.  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES OF AUGUST 28, 2017

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ noted a couple of corrections to the minutes including
  that Lou Persichina was present.

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ

  TO APPROVE THE EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES OF AUGUST 28, 2017
  AS CORRECTED.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  8
SEPTEMBER 26, 2017
 14.  CLOSED SESSION

  NONE

15.  ADJOURNMENT

  At 9:07 p.m. MAYOR ZERUNYAN formally adjourned the City Council meeting to the
  next regular meeting of the City Council scheduled for Monday, October 10, 2017 at
  7:00 p.m.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Heidi Luce  Douglas R. Prichard
City Clerk  City Manager

SEPTEMBER 26, 2017
